The Dallas Times-Herald continues
to fool its readers over bogus census
comparisons between Dallas and
cities that have made no census re
turns.
The Farmers’ alliance has captured
Texas, swallowed the unterrified
democracy and will administer upon
its effects after January 1, 1891.
Great is the democracy but greater
etill is the Alliance.
Responding to the suggestion of
the Light that the Uvalde County
News continue to punch the good
people of that section to put in
acounty exhibit, the News says: “We
can assure our brother of the Light
that the News will do the punching
and hopes yet to see something don e.’
Louisiana Lottery, according to
the compromise, is to be decided by
the white voters of the state, although
it to not so stated in the bill. The
white vote will be taken at the prima
ries apd if the majority vote is against
the reissue of charter the Lottery
company u ill surrender and make no
attempt to carry the mesaure at the
polls.
The beginning of the end of the
Salisbury ministry has come. It has
not come any too soon for Ireland.
If England was as easily stirred up
over outrages in Ireland as she is In
Armenia the Irish iniquity would
Ion" since have come to a perpetual
emff
The Corpus Christi Christian Ad
vocate has a method of dealing with
non-paying church members and non
church attending citizens unknown
to primitive Christianity.” The
Advocate, edited, of course, by a
preacher, says:
“In a short time I am going to pub
lish the names of the members of my
church who have paid to the support
of the church, with the amount each
one has paid from naught up. lam
also going to publish the names of
tnose who attend church with those
who do not attend. Look out now, or
we will locate the “dead-heads.” We
will give you a chance to save your
selves.”
Imagine Christ or Peter or even Paul
posting the members of the little
“First day of the week” companies
who did not bring in their contribu
tions; or sending crieers through the
streets with rolls of papyrus con
taining names of citizens who did not
attend the rooms “where tbe doors
were shut for fear of the Jews.” That
Corpus Christi parson will get him
self into deep water and hot water
both if he carries out his programme.
The people have the same divine
right to stay at home from church as
they have to go to church.

It is three weeks since Mr. Blaine
authorized the denial of the reported
statement that be was hostile to the
McKinley bill, but the Texas Iron
News has not yet found it out. Tbe
reported antagonism of Mr. Blaine’s
views on this and other questions of
public policy io that of the president
and the cabinet generally, is merely
democratic moonshine; all glisten and
n. g.
Houston was swallowed by Galves
ton in the contest over district attor
ney nomination as effectually as it
has been swallowed on the Galveston
appropriation matter. Which is the
dog and which is the tall of tbe con
nection, anyway? Houston yawps
when Galveston is hit, after the same
fashion as tbe 11 t'tle girl’s cat.
Cook cannot hope to make any pro
gress in Texas. The very fact of his
candidacy drives the workingmen of
all classes and grades into the ranks
of Hogg. The democrats made a fatal
mistake in permitting this declared
foe of labor to come to the front.
The impossibility of being in two
places at one and tbe same time was
all that prevented the Light from
accepting the cordial invitation to
attend the breaking of ground on the
Corpus Christi and Brownsville road
on the Fourth of July. Tbe Light
has the most pleasant recollections
of former visits to the city that sits
by the sea, and would have gladly
accepted an invitation to "come
down” on that occasion.
The democracy’ are consoling them
selves with the reflection that Reed
will not over the fifty second
congress. It will be time enough to
explode that hope when the next con
gress meets.
The St. Louis Republic is awfully
sorrry for Blaine because he is over
shadowed in the w hite house, and in
the house and senate. So long as
Blaine is not kicking the Republic
ought not to waste its energies in a
sympathy for which no thanks are
payable. Better keep tbe tears for
the democracy. They will need
them.
Topeka has commenced damming
the river to receive power for gener
ating electric force. Her plant will
be the largest electric plant on this
contiqent and manufacturers will be
the care of that stirring capital. San
Antonio Is also in the swim, or at
least donning her bathing suit for the
plunge.
The Yoakum Graphic, which took
such lively interest in the San An
tonio fair last year, is not abating its
earnestness this season. In its last
issue it says:
Bee county will contest for tbe
SI,OOO premium at the San Antonio
fair. Lavaca and De Witt should de
termine to do likewise and begin
actively and push earnestly to the
end that they show up second to none.
Work could accomplish all desired in
tnis matter.
The Graphic has a good chance now
to do some missionary work for the
fair. Be not weary in well doing and
in due time you will get that $l,OOO,
or some other county will, Lots of
fun in it, even if you die a-trying.
The El Paso Tribune finds the
growing city at the crossing of the
Mexican National into the sister re
public a little too heavy to deal with,
and remarks:
“Laredo is the best advertised and
worst located town in all Texas, and
she seems to glory in the distinction.”
She glories in printer’s ink in a way
to throw any other city in Texas in
the shade, and has some substantial
returns to show for her ink invest
ments. El Paso cannot come in on
the same track with her lower Rio
Grande rival.
There are two things Texas has no
use for this year—Hogg and a railway
commission. The Farmers’ Alliance
is crying for both, and the democracy
seem strongly inclined to humor
them.
The El Paso Tribune, unmindful
of the repeated and authoritative de
nials made to the statement, persists
in saying:
“Word comes from Washington
that Secretary Blaine has declared
against the McKinly bill in strong
terms, and will oppose the measure
to the bitter end.”
Word comes from El Paso that the
Tribune does not know tbe meaning
of a plain statement when it sees one,
or seeing, persists in saying what it
must know to be untrue.
Galveston lobbies $300,000 to get
a $.500,000 appropriation. Where does
the profit come in? Will the Post ac
cept this as another “normau maxim.”
Too Busy to Talk.
The advertising man of tbe Light
dropped in on Wolfson this morning,
but he was too busy to talk, the store
being a perfect bee hive with people.
This shows conclusively that the en
campment will be a great to
our merchants. The reputation
which Mr. Wolfson has for giving
bargains Is what drew such a large
crowd to his store. Visitors to the
city, both ladies and gentlemen,
should avail themselves of the eppor
tuntty to get one of tbe rarest Bar
gains ever shown in the city. (tf)
Engineer Wizner, of the Brazos
work, has some very trenchant re
marks to make in connection with
U. 8. Engineer Ernst’s testimony be

Galveston’s harbor. Ernst does not
figure very well in the summing up
of the Brazos critic, and the senate
will find that criticism mighty inter
esting reading.

A CALL
For a Republican County Conven
tion.

for a state republican convention to as
semble in the city of San Antonio, Texas,
on the 3rd day of September, 1890, the re
publicans of Bexar county are requested
to meet in their several justice precincts
and elect delegates to a county conven
tion to assemble at Mission Garden on
July 19,1890, to elect delegates to thestate
convention, a county chairman and com
mittee, and perform such other business
as may conduce to the benefit of the
party.
The basis of representation shall be ap
portioned among the several justice pre
cincts in the ratio of 100 delegates to Pre
cinct No. 1. embracing the City of San
Antonio and fifty delegates to the country
precincts. T. T. Vander Hoeven,
